verdict.rationale: Claude Code's own docs say Claude can run on a schedule for repeating work, the desktop app can schedule recurring tasks, and long-running cloud sessions can be started and checked later. That is genuine recurring, background automation, not just a one-off action. It is reinforced by CI automation via GitHub Actions/GitLab and MCP channels that react to webhook events while the user is away. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on configuring schedules and triggers (evidence is overview-level), independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled background runs work reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Run Claude on a schedule to automate work that repeats: morning PR reviews, overnight CI failure analysis, weekly dependency audits, or syncing docs after PRs merge.
schedule recurring tasks, and kick off cloud sessions.
Kick off long-running tasks and check back when they're done
In CI, you can automate code review and issue triage with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD.
an MCP server can also act as a channel that pushes messages into your session, so Claude reacts to Telegram messages, Discord chats, or webhook events while you're away
